algorithm_requirements: Nonempty closed convex V subset X subset R^d (algorithm box prints subset sign for V versus X; theorem prints subseteq).
psi:X->R strictly convex and differentiable on int X.
x0 in int X; x0 in V is NOT stated.
At round t, l_t:R^d->(-infinity,+infinity] and V subset dom l_t.
Each x_t is selected from the displayed constrained argmin and loss is paid after receipt and update.
theorem_additions: For t=1,...,T, x_t in int X and l_t subdifferentiable on V.
standing_definitions: Definition6.4 identifies X as dom psi, with nonempty interior; strict convexity presupposes convex X.
Definition2.20 is a global subgradient on R^d, not only a support on V.
Definition2.18 properness and Definition2.16 closedness have their exact extended-real meanings.

horizon_endpoints.T: The printed source uses T rounds, etaT and a maximum over 0,...,T-1, which require a positive finite horizon for that expression. No T=0 convention is printed.
horizon_endpoints.updates: x0 is given, x1,...,xT are updates; no x_(T+1) occurs.
horizon_endpoints.terminal: -B(u;xT)/etaT appears in the proof and is discarded by nonnegativity.
horizon_endpoints.monotonicity: Statement literally includes t=T and thus eta_(T+1), although Algorithm15.8 supplies only eta1,...,etaT and proof uses only t<=T-1. Record this endpoint mismatch; do not silently claim exact textual identity after normalization.
horizon_endpoints.constant_case: eta_t=eta for t=1,...,T and eta>0 inherited. Direct constant-step specialization belongs before the maximum bound.

sequence_semantics: Conditional regret guarantee for a supplied sequence of attained interior updates. Source does not provide a general existence/interiority theorem for all data satisfying just the algorithm Require line. Uniqueness can be derived after establishing strict convexity of the update objective, but does not imply existence.
